call.sequence_note: IMPORTANT: this Drive file contains two separate prospect calls, both abandoned and rescheduled. A call with a prospect named Ryan runs 00:00:00 to 00:08:08 and this one runs 00:09:04 to 00:10:23. This prospect sat in the waiting room for roughly nine minutes while the other call ran, then had 70 seconds before being handed back to a setter.

Derek also appears as the setter on the Brandon Salisbury call the previous day and is named in the Michael x Richard internal call. He is not one of the three known setter codes.

Rebooking was handed back to a setter rather than scheduled live: 'I'm going to have Derek reach out to you tomorrow and coordinate, just because my schedule's up in the air the next couple days here'

outcome.next_step: Derek to contact the prospect the following day to arrange a new time. Nothing booked on the call.

notable.note: Seventy seconds. The prospect waited roughly nine minutes in the waiting room while the rep finished a call that had itself been double-booked, then arrived to a reschedule with no time agreed and a handoff back to a setter, on a day the rep described his own schedule as up in the air. Two prospects lost their slots in the same ten-minute recording. Only a display name was captured, so this record cannot be matched to a CRM entry without the Drive metadata.

quality.notes: Short call, but the final exchange merges both speakers under the rep's label — 'Appreciate you, man. Thank you. All right. You have a blessed one.' contains both sides. Role read from content. There is far too little material here to assess reliability properly.
